images.title: Unlike terms do not combine
images.purpose: Shows that 5w² + 6w cannot be written as 11w², because squares and strips are different kinds of term.
images.composition: One row of five squares and six thin strips across the middle, with a struck out wrong answer beneath. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Five equal teal (#0072B2) squares in a row, each w by w, with the label '5w²' under the group. Then a large '+'. Then six equal amber (#E69F00) thin strips, each w tall and 1 wide, standing in a row, with the label '6w' under the group. Below the whole row, centred, the label '11w²' in grey (#6B7280) with one grey line struck through it, and beside it the label 'unlike terms'. Exactly 5 squares and 6 strips.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Only like terms combine: 5w² + 6w stays as it is.
images.description: Shows that 5w² + 6w cannot be written as 11w², because squares and strips are different kinds of term.
images.context: 5w² + 6w cannot be simplified; mistakes (b) and (c) are both unlike terms added.

image_decisions.why: Adding unlike terms is the most common slip in this set; tiles of different shapes make it concrete.
